newsitem.title: FRANCE: Suspected ETA militants on trial in Paris.
newsitem.headline: Suspected ETA militants on trial in Paris.

text.p: Ten suspected Spanish Basque ETA guerrillas or sympathisers, and five French nationals suspected of sheltering them, went on trial in a Paris court on Tuesday.

The 15, as well as four other suspected ETA (Basque Homeland and Freedom) supporters who will be tried in their absence, face up to 10 years in jail for criminal conspiracy tied to a terrorist objective.
Police rounded up the accused following the detention in Bayonne in southwest France in July 1994 of Pedro Pikabea Ugalde, a presumed leader of the Basque separatists.
Police said their investigation rounded up a commando which had been preparing an attack against King Juan Carlos of Spain in August 1995 at Palma de Majorca.
As ETA guerillas often do, Pikabea refused to answer questions in court on Tuesday, saying: "I do not recognise this court, you do not have the right to try me. I am a fighter."
His companions also refused to speak in court, save for Maria Luz Bella Brengas who said that the Basque separatist militants were being tortured in Spain.
France pledged on Monday to increase cooperation with Spain against ETA rebels, saying it would aggressively pursue leaders of the group on its territory.
French Interior Minister Jean-Louis Debre met his Spanish counterpart Jaime Mayor Oreja in Madrid to discuss joint action against the Basque guerrillas who have stepped up attacks in Spain this year.
The ETA has killed more than 800 people in a 29-year fight for an independent Basque state encompassing parts of southern France and northern Spain.
